proof_summary: An odd integer with power-of-two totient is shown to be a squarefree product of Fermat primes, with the totient exponent equal to the sum of the corresponding distinct powers of two; uniqueness of binary expansion then forces an odd solution at exponent \(2^K\) to be exactly \(F_K\), and hence requires \(F_K\) to be prime. Using \(\varphi(m)<m\), any putative smaller solution in the composite case must satisfy \(\varphi(m)=2^{2^K}\); writing \(m=2^a r\) with \(r\) odd and applying the classification or the bound \(\varphi(r)<r\) forces \(m\ge 2^{2^K+1}\), while \(F_K\) when prime and this power of two otherwise attain the respective bounds.
